chain.label: Flight crew misinterpreted APLC landing distance data
chain.trigger: the flight crew misinterpreted the APLC stopping distance data for MED autobrakes by incorrectly comparing APLC runway data with the landing distance provided on the approach plate for runway 22R

chain.label: Captain intended to achieve an early touchdown to minimize rollout
chain.trigger: the captain was concerned about the airplane's touchdown location on runway 22R and intended to take measures during the landing to achieve an early touchdown and minimize the length of the rollout on the runway after touchdown

caused_by.evidence: the misinterpretation of the APLC data...led the captain to believe that stopping distance would be an issue in the landing

chain.label: Captain's abrupt nose-down elevator input at 17 feet destabilized the flare
chain.trigger: the captain's nose-down elevator input at 17 feet radio altitude (2 seconds before the first touchdown) was consistent with an attempt to control the point of touchdown given his concerns about the runway length

caused_by.evidence: consistent with an attempt to control the point of touchdown given his concerns about the runway length

chain.label: Large, rapid elevator reversals produced a classic pilot-induced oscillation
chain.trigger: the captain made a nearly full nose-up elevator input and a large throttle increase to compensate for the increased sink rate caused by his previous nose-down input...consistent with a 'classic' pilot-induced oscillation (PIO)

caused_by.evidence: he destabilized the flare and established a greater sink rate

chain.label: Captain continued attempting to salvage the landing instead of executing a go-around
chain.trigger: the captain's overcontrol of the airplane during the landing and his failure to execute a go-around from a destabilized flare

caused_by.evidence: a go-around executed by the captain at any time through the touchdown and bounce would have prevented the accident

chain.label: Second touchdown imparted energy into the right MLG 3.2 times the certification limit
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's right MLG experienced an energy input of 1,574,000 ft-lbs during the second touchdown, which was 3.2 times the maximum certification energy

caused_by.evidence: the captain's actions during the 5 seconds preceding the second touchdown established the conditions that led to the right wing failure
a go-around executed by the captain at any time through the touchdown and bounce would have prevented the accident

chain.label: Right wing rear spar fractured and right MLG separated under overload
chain.trigger: the energy transmitted into the right MLG during the second touchdown...was sufficient to fully compress (bottom) the right MLG strut and cause structural failure of the right wing rear spar

caused_by.evidence: 3.2 times the MD-11's maximum certificated landing energy and was sufficient to...cause structural failure of the right wing rear spar

chain.label: Airplane rolled inverted, slid off centerline amid a fuel-fed fire, and was destroyed
chain.trigger: the airplane continued to roll as it slid down the runway, coming to rest inverted about 5,126 feet beyond the runway threshold and about 580 feet to the right of the runway centerline...A fuel-fed fire erupted on impact

caused_by.evidence: the structural failure of the right wing rear spar resulted in the rupture of the right wing fuel tanks and fire

chain.label: All five occupants received minor injuries during the crash and egress
chain.trigger: All five occupants received minor injuries in the crash and during subsequent egress through a cockpit window

caused_by.evidence: All five occupants received minor injuries in the crash and during subsequent egress through a cockpit window
